sentences.text: Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 12.09.2019 passed in MVC No.57/2019 by the Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT-IV at Davangere (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
That on 09.05.2018 there was an accident between a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-17-EV-6515 and tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-27-TA-8624 and KA-27- TA-8625 on Ranebennur to Harihar Road because of which one Prabhugowda traveling in a motor cycled died.
The petitioners are the parents of the said deceased Prabhugowda.

They preferred MVC No.57/2019 under Section 163(A)
of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 as its stood then.
The tribunal was pleaded to award a compensation of Rs.3,79,500/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Not satisfied with the same, the petitioners therein have preferred the appeal.

4. In the course of argument, learned counsel for the appellants as well as the learned counsel for respondent No.4 - Insurance Company submitted that the tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased at Rs.40,000/- per annum while calculating the compensation amount towards 'loss of income of deceased'.

However, it has deducted 50% towards his personal expenses when it ought to have deducted 1/3rd as per schedule II of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 and except that there is no other mistake in the order passed by the Tribunal.

Towards 'loss of income of deceased' the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.4,80,000/- (40,000 x 2/3 x 18) as against Rs.3,60,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads remains intact.

5. Thus, the compensation to the petitioner under different heads is modified as hereunder:-
 AMOUNT AMOUNT Sl. HEAD OF AWARDED BY AWARDED BY No. COMPENSATION THE TRIBUNAL THIS COURT  IN RS. IN RS.
 Loss of income of 1 3,60,000-00 4,80,000-00  deceased 2 Medical expenses 15,000-00 15,000-00 3 Loss of estate 2,500-00 2,500-00 4
Funeral expenses 2,000-00 2,000-00  TOTAL 3,79,500-00 4,99,500-00 Sri.Karibasappa Sannagowdru vs Sri. Beerappakoder on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6399358/
3 6. Thus, the petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.4,99,500 - Rs.3,79,500).

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
ii.

The total compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified and petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,20,000/- over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization.

iii. Respondent No.4 shall pay the enhanced compensation amount to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of the judgment and order.
iv.
Draw modified award accordingly.

SD/-
